channel.title: Small Space Greens
channel.description: How-to guides for small-space gardening and microgreens.

item.title: How to grow microgreens in an apartment: your first tray
item.description: Start one edible microgreen tray in an apartment: crop, footprint, supplies, light, and a source-backed harvest window. Steps cite extension sources.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: Gardening gifts for plant lovers in small spaces
item.description: Gardening gifts for plant lovers and gardeners in a small space. Compare LetPot gardens, True Leaf seed and kits, and one windowsill kit. No prices here.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: Microgreen seeds for beginners: which to buy first
item.description: Microgreen seeds for a first tray: radish, pea, broccoli, and sunflower from True Leaf Market, plus how a sprouting seed collection differs.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: Microgreens kit vs DIY: compare setup and repeat costs
item.description: Compare microgreens kits and DIY setups by what is included, space needed, upfront spending, and repeat costs. Choose the approach that fits your plans.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: Microgreens seed density by crop and tray size
item.description: Look up published microgreen seed rates by crop, see which figures are crop-specific, and scale them to your tray. The calculator uses the same rates.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: Pea shoots vs radish microgreens: which should you grow?
item.description: Choose between pea shoots and radish microgreens using published seed weight, soak time, harvest window, and flavor notes. Seed weights come from Utah State.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: Can you grow microgreens on a windowsill?
item.description: Decide whether your windowsill can grow a tray of microgreens, and when the published guidance says to add a lamp. Measure the sill and watch the stems.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: Starting vegetable seeds in an apartment
item.description: Raise vegetable transplants in an apartment for a balcony or garden, with light, timing, and crops you should not eat as microgreens. Check the cited sources.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: How to bottom water microgreens and seed trays
item.description: Bottom water a microgreen or seed tray: which tray has holes, where the water goes, and when to pour the extra out. Then empty the solid tray.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: The 3-Hour Balcony Salad Garden: What to Grow in Low Sun
item.description: Leafy greens and herbs can work with about 3 hours of direct sun. See pot sizes, container mix, and two balcony layouts matched to the light you measured.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)

item.title: Grow a 3 hour salad on your balcony
item.description: About 3 hours of direct sun is enough for leafy greens. Use two 8 inch lettuce pots plus a small herb pot, and skip radishes on that sun budget.
item.author: ryan@smallspacegreens.com (Ryan Moalemi)
